B. Is this measure already running in Lapland wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure lead to lung cancer being found at an earlier stage, and by how much?
Measure: Symptom awareness campaign (cough over three weeks). A campaign on the English "Be Clear on Cancer" model telling people with a persistent cough to see a doctor. Weak evidence: in England the share found at stage I rose during the campaign months and faded within months, so it has to be repeated every year, and the extra GP visits and chest X-rays cost several times the advertising.
effect_summary_en: The English national campaign raised GP visits for cough by people aged 50 and over by 63% over 8 weeks, but the parts of the paper read did not show the 3.1-point stage I rise.
supported_en: British Journal of Cancer (2015): GP visits for cough rose 63%, and recognition of a 3-week cough as a warning sign rose from 18% to 33%.
not_supported_en: The passages read do not show the stage I shift, how long it lasted, or the 0.8-point yearly average.
in_use_summary_en: No public sign was found of a persistent-cough awareness campaign by Lapha or OYS. OYS runs a low-dose CT screening pilot from January 2026, but it takes only people from North Ostrobothnia, not Lapland.
summary_en: No public sign was found that Lapha or OYS runs a persistent-cough awareness campaign; the OYS screening pilot (from January 2026) is a different measure and takes only North Ostrobothnia residents. A 2015 British Journal of Cancer paper reports a 63% rise in GP visits for cough by people aged 50 and over during England's campaign; the passages read did not show the stage shift.
unanswered_en: No page from Lapha or OYS mentioning a cough campaign was found after three search rounds, and the paper's stage I figures (14.1% to 17.3%) and how long the effect lasted were not seen in the passages read.
